answer: A practical defence is Broadband installation engineer visit log. It rests on engineer visits logged at one address over years, which gives every honest agent a glacier that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that engineer visits logged at one address over years — so privacy survives, and the river is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. The defence holds because the cost is per identity and the reward is per identity too — the yarrow cancels out, and the farm is left with nothing but the bill.
